key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produced denser, harder Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings with approximately 27% lower sliding wear volume than conventional radial-feed APS, but little improvement in normal-impact erosion.
engineering_relevance: HV-APS is a promising process choice for sliding-wear protection of steel components, although its benefits should not be assumed for erosion-dominated service.
method: Sprayed Metco 5241 Cr₃C₂–NiCr powder onto S235 steel using conventional radial-feed APS and axial-feed HV-APS.
Characterized coating microstructure, phases, porosity and microhardness.
Compared erosion at 90° impact and ball-on-disc sliding wear under a 30 N load.
evidence_signal: HV-APS versus APS yielded 6.16% versus 11.99% porosity, 1141 versus 897 HV0.2 hardness, 2.85 versus 3.90 mm³ sliding wear volume, and nearly identical erosion rates of 0.19 versus 0.20 mg/g.
watch_item: The comparison changes both torch technology and powder-feeding geometry, so the improvement cannot be attributed to axial feeding alone.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
